messages:
alex (runtime): Ran a cross-cluster profiling pass this morning. EU->US spillover is causing a subtle latency tail when continuous batching pulls from remote queues. Observed increased KV cache miss rate and a burst of kernel switches around token budgets. TL;DR: cross-zone spill creates larger mixed batches that trigger suboptimal kernel selection. :frowning:
maria (infra): ugh. any numbers?
alex (runtime): 99th went from 180ms -> 320ms for short requests during spill windows. Median unchanged. KV cache miss ratio jumped ~3x for affected requests. Flamegraph attached in perf-bot log.
sam (ml): kernel selection change means we're choosing a different matmul kernel once sequence tokens exceed X? Could be perf cliff from fused-attn->fallback.
jenna (sre): can we limit spillover or add a soft-reserve per-region? We want to avoid cross-zone mixing except when idle.
alex (runtime): Agree. Hypothesis: mixed batches with large token variance force kernel chooser to pick a safe-but-slower kernel and also blow KV-cache locality (remote kvs). Proposed quick experiment: enforce soft-reserve (n slots) per-region + per-region token-budget target so continuous batching only pulls from remote queues if local queue has been idle > T or local batch < min_fill. Also add an override to prefer local kernel-friendly grouping.
maria (infra): config snippet for experiment we'd apply via rollout:```yaml
runtime:
  batching:
    min_fill: 6
    max_delay_ms: 12
    token_budget_per_region: 1200  # tokens per batch from region
    soft_reserve_per_region: 8
    spill_threshold_ms: 200
    allow_spill_after_idle_ms: 250
    affinity: soft
```
alex (runtime): nice. We'll also add a metric: "mixed_kernel_switches" (count when kernel_choice != last_choice) and KV-cache-locality ratio. perf-bot can emit these.
perf-bot: Uploaded flamegraph -> https://perf.internal/runs/1791234567/flame.svg :eyes:
maria (infra): question — will soft_reserve increase p99 under high local load? risk of capacity fragmentation. we need a safety: fallback to global pooling if utilization > 85%.
sam (ml): good call. Also test changing kernel-selector hysteresis: avoid switching kernel unless new_choice wins by > 10% estimated throughput. That should reduce flip-flop under mixed batches.
jenna (sre): schedule A/B with Canary region EU-west and control region EU-central. Run 2h ramp at 50% traffic. Collect p50/p90/p99, mixed_kernel_switches, kv_locality, and fail-open rate.
alex (runtime): I'll own the rollout + perf dashboards. Plan: implement soft_reserve + token_budget + kernel hysteresis in runtime (small patch), enable metrics, canary tomorrow 08:00 UTC. If p99 improves and CPU/GPU utilization delta within 5%, promote.
maria (infra): note: also check cost impact — batching changes could change token efficiency. Track tokens-per-second and net token-cost.
sam (ml): one more thing: when a batch contains requests with very different max_tokens, consider a split heuristic: chunk off short sequences into a micro-batch and keep long tails separate. That reduces variance in seq length. Could be enabled as opt-in.
alex (runtime): adding that to the backlog; it might require KV cache handling changes. For now soft_reserve + token_budget + kernel hysteresis first.
jenna (sre): sounds good. ping me when canary starts; I'll validate SLO and open incident runbook if regressions hit.
alex (runtime): will do. thanks all :thumbsup:
